later_events.mechanism: statutory_repeal_of_code_approval_and_enforcement_provisions: S.J. Res. 113 section 2, approved June 14, 1935, repealed the provisions of Title I delegating power to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for their enforcement; a later event of this denial, which was already exhausted on November 4, 1933.

clauses.reason: The order's only command is "do order that the application for exemption by the above-named applicants be and it is hereby denied". A denial of an application for exemption commands nothing after it issues; its command was performed on the date it was signed, November 4, 1933 (reviewed shared analysis), and no later effective date is stated. The repeal of the code-approval and enforcement provisions by S.J. Res. 113 section 2 on June 14, 1935 is a later event that ended the code's own operation, not an end of this denial.

research_rationale:
The held American Presidency Project transcription of EO:6403 (signed November 4, 1933; the page heading names the application of Kaplan Brothers) records that a Code of Fair Competition for the Artificial Flower and Feather Industry "has been heretofore approved by me", that hearings were granted to the applicants, and that no case of injustice and extreme hardship was made out. The only command is "do order that the application for exemption by the above-named applicants be and it is hereby denied". Under the reviewed shared analysis, an order that denies an application for exemption from a code commands nothing after it issues: its command is exhausted by performance on the date it is signed, and the applicant's continuing obligation is the code's own operation, which the approving order governs and which ended with the repeal on June 14, 1935 (S.J. Res. 113 section 2, "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed"). The repeal is therefore a later event of this order, not its end.

savings.reason: The denial was performed on the date it was signed, so nothing remains to be saved from it; the applicants' obligations after the denial arose from the code, which the approving order governed and which was repealed on June 14, 1935 (SUPPLEMENT:SJRES113). Acts done and liabilities incurred under the code before the repeal are accrued, and the section 5 exemption for completed action is an accrued effect (SUPPLEMENT:NIRA5).
